content.text:
I submitted **index 0 (Fe 0.87 / Sb 0.13)** as the best composition, with a measured EQE of 0.162%. That is the top of only three merit measurements across 30 compositions, so I can't rule out a better one I didn't measure.

**What I measured (all 3 merit measurements used):**

| Index | Fe fraction | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|
| 14 | 0.52 | about 0 (−0.006) |
| 3 | 0.82 | 0.106 |
| 0 | 0.87 | 0.162 |

**How the choice was made:**
- **First pick failed.** I started at index 14, the closest match to FeSbO4. The models favoured it: MEGNet predicts a band gap of 2.08 eV, just under the 2.1 eV light, and MACE puts it on the stability hull. It produced essentially no photoresponse.
- **XRD (2 of 5 used)** showed the same rutile FeSbO4-type pattern at both the Fe-rich end (index 2) and the Sb-rich end (index 27). The phase present doesn't explain the difference in EQE, so I followed the composition trend instead.
- **EQE rises as Fe increases.** Index 0 is at the edge of the library, so the best composition is probably at or near index 0. Index 3 was a check for a peak inside the range and came in lower.
- **Sb-rich side not measured.** EQE was already falling as Sb increased, and FeSb2O4 is predicted at 2.38 eV, above the photon energy. This is inferred, not measured.

**Main caveat:** the model predictions were a poor guide here. MEGNet's Fe2O3 gap ranged from 0.81 to 2.77 eV depending on the setting, and the one confident "good" prediction (index 14) was the worst result. The choice rests on the three measurements, not the models.
